title: Vocabulary & Language
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah memiliki pengetahuan dasar untuk menyebutkan kegiatan yang biasa mereka lakukan di waktu luang.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 56-58
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will learn new words about fun activities and places they can go in their free time.
Learners will be able to understand, identify, and say key vocabulary about fun activities and places.
Learners will be able to make invitations using Let’s …, How about …?, and Would you like to …?, and accept or refuse them politely.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes a letter on the board (e.g. S).

Ask the students whose name starts with the shown letter to stand up, introduce themselves, and say one thing they like to do on the weekend (e.g. “My name is Sinta. I like to go swimming on the weekend.”). Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 56.

Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to talk about what they can see in the pictures (e.g. kids playing volleyball at the beach, friends walking at the shopping center). Ask them to write down any English words they know about the topic in their notebooks.
Elicit some ideas from the groups and write down any key words on the board.

Read the questions on the page together (e.g. “What are some fun activities to do near your house?”, “What is your favorite thing to do after school?”). The teacher can model his/her own answers and write them on the board or show them on the screen.
Tell students they have 5-6 minutes to discuss the questions. Encourage them to use English, but if they don’t have enough vocabulary, it’s acceptable to use some words in their first language.
After 5-6 minutes, stop the task and elicit some ideas from students. Tell them that by the end of Unit 7 they will be able to answer questions like these more easily.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 57 and ask the class, “What can you see on the page?”
Tell students that they will do a listening task. They need to listen and write the number in each box according to the order they hear the words in the audio.

Before playing the audio, read all of the words together: the mall, the food court, go shopping, see an exhibition, the stadium, watch a concert, attend a festival, go to a convention. Ask simple questions to check understanding, e.g. “Where can we watch a soccer game?”
Play audio 7.1. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, then play the audio again.
Check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the sentences from the audio script aloud, in pairs (e.g. “My father and I went to the stadium to watch a soccer game.”).
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the words they hear.

Play audio 7.2 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio. Check to make sure all students are repeating the vocabulary.
Pay attention to the longer phrases such as “see an exhibition” and “go to a convention”, and drill them again if needed.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
Ask students to look in their books at the Vocabulary C task and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Remind students to look for clues in each sentence to help them choose the correct word or phrase from the vocabulary.
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do (Answer: go to a convention).
Put students in pairs and ask them to complete the task in around 5 minutes.

Then, check the answers (2. the stadium, 3. go shopping, 4. watch a concert, 5. attend a festival, 6. go to the food court). Write the answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the completed sentences aloud to each other, in pairs.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Ask students to write the eight vocabulary items in order, from what they like to do or where they like to go most (1) to what they like least (8).
Put students in groups of four and ask them to compare their lists by asking each other questions.
Write these questions on the board to guide students:
Where do you like to go? / Where don’t you like to go?
What do you like to do? / What don’t you like to do?
What is number 1 on your list? Why do you like to go shopping?
Give students about 10 minutes, then elicit some responses from each group, e.g. “What do people like to do in your group?” and “Where don’t people like to go in your group?”
Ask students to open their Student Book to page 58.
First, the teacher reads the Q&A models in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the Q&A models aloud as a class.
Then, the teacher asks students to read the Q&A models together in pairs (Read with a friend).

This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs. Encourage students to change the key vocabulary in the invitations, by using the vocabulary learned on the previous page (e.g. “Let’s go to the food court!”, “How about we go shopping?”, “Would you like to watch a concert?”).

Explain that the invitations have different levels of formality: Let’s … is friendly and used with friends, How about …? is a casual suggestion, and Would you like to …? is polite and used with people we don’t know well.
Point out ways to accept (Great! / OK, let’s go! / Yes, I would like to …) and to refuse politely (No, sorry. I would not like to … / No, thanks. I don’t want to …).

Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes, e.g. “Let’s to go shopping” and “How about go to the mall?”). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at the practice task B on Student Book page 58.

Point out that students need to write a question or sentence that is an invitation to go somewhere or do something. They should look at the answer to find clues, and use the Language Box at the bottom of the page to help them.
Put students in pairs and give them around 5 minutes to complete the task, then ask them to check their answers with a new partner.
Elicit answers from the class and write them on the board. Answers may vary, e.g. “Would you like to go see an exhibition?”, “Let’s go shopping!”, “How about we go to the stadium?”

Ask students to practice asking and answering the questions in pairs. First, Student A invites and Student B answers. Then, switch roles. Tell them to focus on pronunciation and intonation so they sound more natural.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Put students in pairs and write the key vocabulary from Student Book page 57 on the board.
Write the invitation starters on the board: Let’s …, How about …?, Would you like to …?
Ask students to take turns inviting each other to go to the places and do the activities on the board, using all three invitation forms. Their partner can accept or refuse the invitation politely.
Before each short conversation, students choose who they are (e.g. two friends, mother and son, grandparent and grandchild) so they can choose the most suitable invitation.
Write an example on the board:
A (friend): Let’s go to the mall after school!
B (friend): OK, let’s go!
A (student): Would you like to see an exhibition with us, Mrs. Rina?
B (teacher): No, thanks. I don’t want to go today.
Give students about 10 minutes, then elicit some invitations and responses from pairs of students. Give positive and corrective feedback as needed.
Choose 1-2 students to invite a classmate to do a fun activity this weekend using one of the invitation forms they have learned, and ask the classmate to accept or refuse politely.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: pengamatan pelafalan saat drill kosakata (listen and repeat).
Pemeriksaan jawaban latihan kosakata dan language practice di Student Book.
Unjuk kerja lisan: peserta didik memakai kosakata & struktur baru dalam kalimat sendiri.

Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
